item.title: Centre County Man Reported Missing Located and Is Safe
item.description: Updated 10:48 a.m. Jan. 12 A Centre County man who was reported missing on Sunday has been found and is safe, according to state police at Rockview. Robert Fohringer, 87, of Centre Hall, had been reported missing after he was last seen at about 11 a.m. Sunday in the area of Earlystown Road (Route 45) in Potter Township, according to a missing endangered person advisory. item.title: Bellefonte Area Company Now Employee-Owned
item.description: The employees of a Bellefonte area company are now its owners. SilcoTek, based in the Benner Township, became employee-owned on Jan. 1 through the creation of an Employee Stock Ownership Plan, according to a release. item.title: ‘Joe Dirt’ Tribute Takes Top Prize in Pennsylvania Farm Show Mullet Contest
item.description: HARRISBURG, Pa. (AP) — A packed crowd celebrated the much-maligned but enduring mullet hairstyle Monday in a contest at the Pennsylvania Farm Show in Harrisburg. The short-in-the-front, long-in-the-back coiffure, once the province of Canadian hockey players and hair metal bands, attracted about 150 competitors and more than a thousand spectators for the day's “mane” attraction. item.description: The next stop in Beau Pribula's college career has been revealed. item.title: State College Council Sets Process for Filling Vacancy Following Portney’s Resignation
item.description: State College Borough Council on Monday formally accepted the resignation of one of its members and agreed on a process for selecting his replacement. Josh Portney announced last week that he planned to resign from council effective at midnight on Tuesday. A Penn State Law student and the youngest member of council, he stepped down because he has accepted a clerkship with Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court.
